turns.teacher: Exactly, Saanvi—one bundle is ten, and loose sticks show the extra ones. If a number has three loose sticks, how many extras are there?

end.parentNote: Saanvi practised making teen numbers with one bundle of ten and some loose sticks, and writing the digits in the correct order. They wrote 14 correctly and used the bundle-and-loose-ones method once. They mixed up counting the bundle as 1 instead of 10 when finding the total, and this was not corrected by the end. At home, use a bundle of 10 pencils and a few single pencils; ask, “How many in all?” and count the bundle as ten.
